chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra and Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding a woman who has a slave husband, so his master died and she inherited him, he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no marriage between the two of them'.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a free woman and her slave husband if she inherits him after his master's death?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the marital bond is dissolved rather than merely suspended when a free woman inherits her slave husband, as the resulting master-slave hierarchy creates a structural impediment to the marriage contract. This highlights the Shia juristic principle that social status and ownership dynamics directly influence the validity of nikah, distinguishing this case from scenarios where the husband is manumitted. The decision underscores the importance of maintaining clear social distinctions within the family unit in classical Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sayf Bin Ameyra and Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said regarding a woman for whom there was a slave husband. So his master died, and she inherited him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no marriage between the two of them’.
